title: How to cut toenails properly
intro: Cutting toenails the right way helps prevent painful ingrown nails, infections and pressure problems. A few simple habits, such as cutting straight across and not too short, protect your feet. People with diabetes, poor circulation or reduced sensation need extra care and often benefit from professional foot care.

sections.heading: Preparing to cut
paragraphs: Wash your feet and make sure the nails are dry but not rock hard. Softening nails after a short foot bath, then drying thoroughly, makes them easier to trim. Use good light and sit comfortably so that you can see what you are doing.

sections.heading: The right technique
paragraphs: Use clean nail clippers or nail scissors with straight blades designed for toenails. Cut straight across and leave a small free edge of about one millimetre of white nail. Do not round the corners or cut deep into them, since this encourages nails to grow into the skin.
Smooth sharp edges with a nail file, working gently from the side toward the centre. Avoid cutting the cuticle or poking under the nail with sharp tools.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Cutting nails too short, rounding the corners, tearing nails or picking at them can cause skin injury and ingrown nails. Shoes that are too tight, especially narrow toe boxes, press on the nail and add to the problem.

sections.heading: Extra care for some people
paragraphs: If you have diabetes, nerve damage, poor circulation or poor eyesight, do not cut thick or hard nails yourself, and do not treat corns or calluses with blades or chemical plasters. Check your feet every day, including between the toes, and see a podiatrist or doctor if you find redness, blisters, wounds or colour changes.
Thickened, discoloured or crumbly nails may signal a fungal infection or other problem and should be assessed rather than hidden with polish.

sections.heading: When to get help
paragraphs: See a healthcare professional for a painful, red or swollen nail edge, pus, fever, or a nail that is growing into the skin. Do not try to cut out an ingrown nail yourself if it is inflamed.

examples.title: Setting a routine
examples.text: Imagine you trim your nails whenever they snag your socks. You could instead set a monthly reminder, trim straight across after a bath, file the edges, and check the skin around each nail as you do.

examples.title: Seeing a podiatrist
examples.text: Suppose you have diabetes and your toenails have become thick. You might ask your doctor about referral to a foot specialist for regular care and learn which daily foot checks to carry out at home.
